inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL UPDATE JOIN derives one latest related record per entity through a grouped MAX date subquery and writes the resulting owner into the entity table.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an independently authored asset assignment refresh. A grouped MAX event-day subquery identifies each unit's latest owner event, an outer join resolves the corresponding owner, and UPDATE JOIN changes only units with a latest event while leaving an unobserved unit unchanged.

fixture_notes: Units 3001 and 3002 receive owners from their latest event days; unit 3003 has no event and retains its NULL owner.
determinism_notes: Each unit has one event on its maximum day, so the grouped latest-owner join has no ties. All IDs, dates, and owners are fixed; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE asset_units (unit_id INT PRIMARY KEY, unit_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, owner_id INT NULL)
CREATE TABLE asset_owner_events (event_id INT PRIMARY KEY, unit_id INT NOT NULL, owner_id INT NOT NULL, event_day INT NOT NULL)
INSERT INTO asset_units VALUES (3001, 'north shed', NULL), (3002, 'east shed', 77), (3003, 'west shed', NULL)

steps.sql: UPDATE asset_units AS u JOIN (SELECT e.unit_id, e.owner_id FROM asset_owner_events AS e JOIN (SELECT unit_id, MAX(event_day) AS latest_day FROM asset_owner_events GROUP BY unit_id) AS latest ON e.unit_id = latest.unit_id AND e.event_day = latest.latest_day) AS latest_owner ON u.unit_id = latest_owner.unit_id SET u.owner_id = latest_owner.owner_id

checks.sql: SELECT unit_id, unit_name, owner_id FROM asset_units ORDER BY unit_id
SELECT event_id, unit_id, owner_id, event_day FROM asset_owner_events ORDER BY event_id
